scope_note: When the host owns the cache (a harness), do-it cannot touch the prefix (research/09 section 7 item 1); these rules then govern only brief layout, spawn grouping, tier and model change timing, and telemetry.

rules.statement: Static instructions and tools first, volatile content last; no timestamps, ids or git status in the system block or early blocks.
History is append-only; never edit, reorder or summarise earlier messages in place; compact only as a fork that reuses the parent prefix.
Sort tools by name and keep JSON key order stable in every request.
Never add or remove tools mid-session; mask through tool_choice, allowed tools or state messages.
Never switch model mid-session; hand off through a fresh session with a written brief at a spawn boundary.
Updates (time, changed files, orchestrator state) go in the next user message or tool result, not the system prompt.
Do not change thinking, effort, tool_choice, images or speed settings mid-thread.
Issue one warming request per provider, model and prefix, wait for its first response, then parallelise sibling workers.
Use the 1 hour TTL when the expected gap exceeds 5 minutes and at least two reuses are expected; lifetime counts from request start.
Place no cache markers below the model's minimum prefix; sub-minimum prefixes do not cache and the write premium is wasted.

always.statement: Log read, write and uncached tokens per call; hit rate is read over read plus write plus uncached; ignore sessions under 20 requests.
